Label: Index date
Definition (Validated from Protocol): Date of the patient's earliest qualifying multiple myeloma diagnosis date during the identification period.
Additional Notes (Validated from Protoco: Patients are required to have at least 1 inpatient medical claim with a diagnosis code for MM in any position (ICD-9-CM=203.0x or ICD-10-CM code=C90.0x) or at least 2 outpatient medical claims for MM in any position on the claim, on separate days within 90 days, during the identification period. Patients with 2 claims 30 or 60 days apart will also be flagged for consideration. The index date is the date of the first medical claim for MM within the identification period. Diagnosis codes for MM are in tab 42 'MM dx code'. As data in Optum CDM is collected primarily for health insurance and not research purposes, all MM diagnosis codes are to be considered and the code list will not be limited to those specifically indicated for newly diagnosed MM. Flags should also be made to distinguish which claims are non-diagnostic claims. A non-diagnostic claim refers to a claim for treatment of a condition (e.g., infusion) rather than diagnosis (see tab 49 'Diagnostic') (Protocol Section 4.2, Inclusion Criterion 1).
Discrepancy Found in Original Program Sp: No discrepancy found. Aligned with protocol.

Label: Baseline period
Definition (Validated from Protocol): The baseline period is fixed and is the six months before the index date.
Additional Notes (Validated from Protoco: Patients must have six months of continuous enrollment (CE) with medical AND pharmacy benefits before the index date. Patients with gaps in enrollment of <=30 days are considered to be continuously enrolled. The purpose of the baseline is to create a period during which patients who were previously diagnosed with MM are identified; if treated in the baseline period, these patients will be excluded (see Exclusion Criteria). If not treated in the baseline period, these patients will be assumed to be smoldering until the point of treatment in the follow-up period (Protocol Section 4.2, Inclusion Criterion 3).
Discrepancy Found in Original Program Sp: Original program spec said 'medical or pharmacy benefits'. Protocol (Section 4.2, Criterion 3) states 'medical and pharmacy benefits'. Changed 'or' to 'and'.

Label: Follow up period
Definition (Validated from Protocol): The follow-up period begins on the index date and is variable-length, ending at the earliest of death, health plan disenrollment, or the end of the study period (30June2025).
Additional Notes (Validated from Protoco: Patients are only required to have >=1 day of CE starting on the index date until death or study period end. Patients with gaps in enrolment of <=30 days are considered to be continuously enrolled; consider medical and/or pharmacy benefits. Note: Patients with >=3 months of CE with medical or pharmacy benefits from the index date (with no allowable gaps in enrollment), or who have an assigned date of death <3 months after the index date, will be flagged for consideration for sensitivity or secondary analyses, ending on the earliest of health plan disenrollment or the study period end. For patients with an assigned date of death <3 months after the index date, these patients are retained and have a limited follow-up period that ends at the assigned date of death (Protocol Section 4.2, Inclusion Criterion 4).

Protocol (Section 4.2, Criterion 4) specifies the follow-up ends at the earliest of death, health plan disenrollment, or end of study period. Label: Eligibility cohort - smoldering MM
Definition (Validated from Protocol): Study team does not want to exclude smoldering MM patients. Optum built study cohort with the intention to exclude smoldering MM patients.
Additional Notes (Validated from Protoco: The team will additionally include patients who had >=1 non-diagnostic medical claim for MM during the baseline period. These patients were excluded by Optum originally. If a patient has newly diagnosed or active MM, it would be likely that they would experience frequent activity, hence why we look for 2 non-diagnostic MM claims close together in the first step of the attrition table. A smoldering patient would have infrequent activity, hence why a claim for MM that falls outside of the 30, 60, or 90 days window requirement used to identify newly diagnosed patients is likely a smoldering patient. Study team will consider excluding patients with a standalone treatment code (rather than any non-diagnostic code) on an MM claim in the baseline period for future sensitivity analysis. This would not remove smoldering patients but rather ensure our patients were newly active MM patients (Protocol Section 4.2; Appendix C).
Discrepancy Found in Original Program Sp: No discrepancy found. Consistent with protocol language in Section 4.2 regarding baseline criteria and Appendix C pressure-testing criteria.

Label: Inpatient vs non-inpatient classification
Definition (Validated from Protocol): A claim is classified as inpatient using two approaches in combination (OR logic) per Optum CDM business rules guidance.
Additional Notes (Validated from Protoco: Approach 1 (POS/TOS): Inpatient if POS IN (21, 51, 61) OR TOS_CD IN ('FAC_IP.ACUTE', 'FAC_IP.REHSNF', 'PROF.INPVIS', 'FAC_IP.SNF'). Approach 2 (CONF_ID): Inpatient if CONF_ID is NOT NULL and validated against T_CONFINEMENT table with both ADMIT_DATE and DISCH_DATE present. Non-inpatient: All records not meeting either approach above. A claim is classified as inpatient if either approach identifies it as inpatient. This maximizes capture of true inpatient encounters. Rationale: Using both approaches together provides the most comprehensive inpatient identification.
